t.1.74.1: O Rāma, son of Daśaratha, O hero, your wondrous valor is heard of, and the breaking of the bow too has been heard by me in full.
t.1.74.2: That breaking of the bow by you was wondrous and beyond imagining; having heard of it, I have come here, bringing another splendid bow.
t.1.74.3: Here is this great bow of Jāmadagnya, dreadful in appearance; draw it to the full with an arrow and display your own strength.
t.1.74.4: Therefore, once I have seen your strength in fully drawing this bow, I shall grant you a single combat, a fitting tribute to your valour.
t.1.74.5: Having heard those words of his, King Daśaratha then, with a downcast face, dejected and with joined palms, spoke these words.
t.1.74.6: You, greatly renowned one of brahmin lineage, now calmed from your wrath against the kṣatriyas, ought to grant freedom from fear to my young sons.
t.1.74.7: Born in the family of the Bhārgavas, who are devoted to Vedic study and religious vows, you laid down your weapon after making a solemn promise before Sahasrākṣa.
t.1.74.8: Having become devoted to dharma, you gave the earth to Kāśyapa, went to the forest, and made your dwelling on Mount Mahendra.
t.1.74.10: While Daśaratha was speaking thus, the mighty Jāmadagnya, utterly disregarding those words, addressed Rāma alone.
t.1.74.9: You have come, great sage, for the utter destruction of me and mine; for if Rāma alone is slain, none of us will live.
t.1.74.11: These two bows were the finest, divine and renowned throughout the worlds, firm, mighty and foremost, well crafted by Viśvakarman.
t.1.74.13: This second bow, the invincible one belonging to Viṣṇu, was given by the foremost of the gods; and this bow, O Kākutstha, is equal in strength to the bow of Rudra.
t.1.74.14: Then all the deities asked the Grandsire, wishing to ascertain the relative strength and weakness of the blue-throated one and of Viṣṇu.
t.1.74.12: One of them, the destroyer of Tripura, was bestowed by the gods upon Tryambaka when he was eager for battle, and it is that bow, O best of men, O Kākutstha, which was broken by you.
t.1.74.15: Understanding the intention of the gods, the Grandsire, best among the truthful, created enmity between the two of them.
t.1.74.16: And in that conflict there arose a great, hair-raising battle between Śitikaṇṭha and Viṣṇu, each seeking victory over the other.
t.1.74.18: Then the gods, having assembled together with hosts of seers and with the Cāraṇas, entreated them, and those two foremost of gods there became pacified.
t.1.74.17: Then that bow of Śiva, of fearsome might, was slackened, and the three-eyed Mahādeva was held motionless by a mere roar of 'huṃ'.
t.1.74.19: Seeing that bow of Śiva rendered slack by the might of Viṣṇu, the gods together with the hosts of sages then deemed Viṣṇu the greater.
t.1.74.20: But the greatly renowned Rudra, though enraged, placed the bow together with its arrow in the hand of the royal sage Devarāta among the Videhas.
t.1.74.21: And this bow of Viṣṇu, O Rāma, the conqueror of enemy cities, Viṣṇu himself gave to Ṛcīka the Bhārgava as a supreme trust.
t.1.74.22: The greatly radiant Ṛcīka then gave the divine bow to his son, my father, the great-souled Jamadagni, whose deeds were beyond compare.
t.1.74.23: When my father, endowed with the power of austerity, had laid down his weapons, Arjuna, resorting to a base and vulgar mind, brought about his death.
t.1.74.24: But having heard of the unworthy and most dreadful slaying of my father, out of rage I went on exterminating the kṣatriyas many times over, each time they were born anew.
t.1.74.25: And having won the entire earth, O Rāma, I then, at the end of the sacrifice, gave it as the sacrificial fee to the great-souled Kāśyapa, whose deeds are meritorious.
t.1.74.26: Having given it away, I made my dwelling on Mahendra, endowed with the power of austerity; hearing of the breaking of the bow, I have come here in haste.
t.1.74.27: Therefore, Rāma, holding the duty of a kṣatriya foremost, take up this great and excellent bow of Viṣṇu, which has come down from father and grandfather.
t.1.74.28: Set upon this finest of bows an arrow that conquers the cities of foes, if you are able, O Kākutstha; then I will grant you single combat.
